facts.fact: The Ministry of Public Health's plan describes DHIS2 as the ministry's national system for collecting aggregate health data, implemented by its Health Information Unit; no date is attached, so the plan's published date is used.

The National Digital Health Strategic Plan 2020-2024 sets objective 5.2, an integrated national HMIS management system in 70% of health facilities by 2024, and costs under it the integration of parallel data collection systems into the national system, hosting fees for the national data platform (XAF 30 million over five years) and internet fees for 190 health districts and 10 regions (XAF 300 million); dated to the plan's publication.

The ministry's plan states that DHIS2 enables data sharing between the health districts and the central level, with flow mainly one way, and budgets internet connection for data management and data entry training for health districts and regions only, not for facilities; no date is attached, so the published date is used.

The ministry's table of applications gives DHIS 2-CIS as scaled up in all districts, covering about 6,000 facilities, for compiling indicators at district, regional and national level; it gives no count or share of facilities entering their own reports. The table is undated, so the published date is used.

The ministry's plan, citing a February 2018 assessment prepared for the US CDC, gives the OpenMRS-based Bahmni electronic medical record as implemented in 0 facilities, with planning under way for 10 sites.

The ministry's plan, citing a February 2018 assessment prepared for the US CDC, counts 0 facilities implementing the Bahmni electronic medical record; it lists among weaknesses the absence of a unified patient record and of a unique patient identifier.

The ministry's plan, citing a February 2018 assessment prepared for the US CDC, names one partner, ICAP, as the user of the Bahmni electronic medical record, which it describes as locally configured for the Cameroon health system.

The National Digital Health Strategic Plan 2020-2024 costs the expansion of the electronic medical record under objective 5.2: mapping existing patient software, a consultant to develop an interoperable record (XAF 45 million), user training at 3,000 health facilities (XAF 600 million) and installation in 3,000 facilities at XAF 150 million a year; dated to the plan's publication.

The plan also lists as weaknesses low allocation of financial resources to the health information system, absence of interoperability and of a regulatory framework for electronic medical records, and as a strength the existence of a national system collecting individual patient data, which it does not name; no finance fact is taken because the passages do not show the plan's financing section.
